items.caption:
Jensen Huang says one gigawatt of AI data center costs about $50 billion.

The Nvidia CEO adds that once the components ship, they pass through an OEM and land at the data center, and getting it running from there could take four to six months.

Is $50 billion per gigawatt a sensible bet or too much, too fast?

Source: Yahoo Finance, Nvidia’s CEO on the AI debt scare, China, and jobs (full interview). Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=sH5qyeHSdVs

items.caption:
Jensen Huang says 80% of AI-native startups are using open models.

His point: you can take an open model that is close to the frontier, post-train it with your own expertise and data, make it very good at your domain, and build a company around it.

If you were starting an AI company today, would you build on an open model or a closed one?

Source: Yahoo Finance, Nvidia’s CEO on the AI debt scare, China, and jobs (full interview). Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=sH5qyeHSdVs

items.caption:
Jensen Huang says China manufactures AI researchers at scale.

The Nvidia CEO says that if one country can manufacture things at scale, chips, open models and, very importantly, AI researchers, nobody does it more seriously, at a larger scale or better than China.

Which matters more in the AI race: chips, models or people?
